rationale: A wins because it does the harder newsroom work: it turns REI's tidy announcement into testable tensions instead of only friendly service and trend pitches. Its strongest line, "REI won't say how big its resale business actually is, even as it leans on it for sustainability credit," uses a supplied hole as the story; B's "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" imports a premise the update never gave us. B is clean, but clean is not the same as sharp.
gaps_in_A: "the dividend flows to paying customer-members, not to the employees organizing" smuggles in "paying" and assumes a neat member-versus-worker split the update does not establish.
"announced alongside the dividend as of today" overstates the timing. The update says the dividend was issued this year; it does not clearly say the dividend and rollout were announced the same day.

"REI's bet: gear resale and repair aren't a sustainability side project, they're core retail infrastructure" overlaps with the first rollout angle and needs outside category proof before it earns that altitude.

"None of these are pitch-ready yet -- the strongest three (labor tension, sustainability disclosure, co-op mechanics)" wrongly sidelines the straightforward retail-ops story and treats a hostile labor frame as one of the main paths.
gaps_in_B: "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" is invented context. Useful thesis, bad foundation.
"The sustainability angle on REI's resale expansion" as a "duplicate" is a miss. The undisclosed used-gear sales share is a separate accountability story, not merely paragraph two of the trend piece.
"Record dividend lands amid union drives..." as "off-beat" overcorrects. It may be a defensive angle rather than a proactive pitch, but a strategist still has to surface it cleanly.
"repair counter in every store" decorates the fact. The update says repairs are available at all stores; it does not say each store has a dedicated counter.
